# Parley v0.1.56

Fixes for running panes' relay permissions and Git worktree discovery.

## Running panes keep their launch permissions

Editing or deleting a custom permission profile no longer changes the relay
ticket requirement of an already-running Codex pane. The requirement now
uses the effective profile captured for that pane's launch generation,
matching the permissions its process received. Profile edits take effect
on the next start or explicit restart.

Host Codex permission rules also explicitly allow reading the exact ticket
socket and its canonical path alias for the shim's pre-connect check,
without granting access to sibling pane endpoints. This is a defensive
permission change: it has not been established as the cause or a verified
fix for the reported “ticket required” failure.

## Worktree paths with line breaks

Git worktree discovery now preserves NUL field boundaries. Literal line
breaks in a path or lock reason no longer truncate the path or turn part of
the value into another record. The regression coverage includes a real Git
worktree with newline, carriage-return and tab characters in its name.

## Verification

The merged fixes passed 379 native checks, 54 script tests, both repository
scans and the native build in the GitLab Tart VM. The two Docker-only
checks were explicitly skipped because the VM has no Docker runtime.
Thirteen targeted native checks and the build also passed locally and in
an independent Claude review. The isolated sandbox comparison needed to
confirm a prior socket metadata refusal remains unverified.

The GitLab release workflow must pass its deterministic checks, native
build, 25-round eight-pane Ghostty soak, packaging, launch verification and
checksum checks before publishing. Its two Docker-only checks are explicitly
skipped because the Tart VM has no Docker runtime.

Unnotarized test beta, as before. Permission changes reach new or explicitly
restarted panes after updating; Parley does not restart existing panes
automatically.
